newsitem.title: INDIA: Delhi shares boosted by pension rule changes.
newsitem.headline: Delhi shares boosted by pension rule changes.

text.p: A revival of buying by foreign institutional investors coupled with purchases made by mutual funds on news of modifications in private pension fund rules drove Delhi shares to a higher close, brokers said.
The Delhi Stock Exchange's sensitive index closed 6.11 points higher at 742.95.
"It seems that operators have resumed their buying activity at current prices," said Vikas Sharma of brokers B.B. Portfolio.
On Monday the government announced it had taken steps to allow private pension funds to earn more on their investments.
The government said it had partially modified the investment pattern applicable to non-government provident, superannuation and gratuity funds so that the funds could earn more on investments.
Effective on October 1, the government will reduce the required limit in special deposits to 20 percent from 30 percent, it said.

The investment in bonds or securities of public financial institutions, public sector companies and certificates of deposits of public sector banks has been increased to 40 percent from 30 percent, the government statement said.
Reliance Industries firmed 2.35 rupees to 196.45 on institutional buying, brokers said.
TELCO rose five rupees to 455 on fund buying as speculators covered short positions, they said.
Hindustan Lever surged 15 rupees to 825, and ITC quoted 8.15 rupees higher at 288.25.
Larsen and Toubro gained 2.25 rupees to 240.50.
